title: GI bleeding and stress ulcer prophylaxis

steps.tx: A **Glasgow-Blatchford score** of 0 or 1 identifies very low risk upper gastrointestinal bleeding that can often avoid admission. **Rockall scoring** needs the endoscopy and is not the admission score. Pre-endoscopic risk stratification identifies stable patients who can safely undergo outpatient evaluation, directing hospital admission to high-risk presentations.

steps.tx: **Villanueva** showed that a restrictive **transfusion threshold** of 7 g/dL improved outcomes compared with a liberal threshold in upper gastrointestinal bleeding. Massive bleeding and ischaemic heart disease are the debated exceptions. Liberal transfusion elevates portal venous pressures, provokes clot disruption, and significantly increases rebleeding and 45-day all-cause mortality.

rows: Trigger transfusion only when Hb under 7 g/dL
95% survival; lower rebleeding and fewer adverse events
Trigger transfusion when Hb under 9 g/dL
Over-transfusion distends bleeding varices and disrupts clots

steps.tx: After endoscopic haemostasis of a high risk ulcer, an intravenous **proton pump inhibitor** is given. The examined continuous regimen is 80 mg then 8 mg per hour for 72 hours. Intermittent high dose therapy is an acceptable alternative. Maintaining gastric pH above 6 stabilizes platelet aggregation and prevents fibrin clot dissolution by pepsin.

left.title: High-dose continuous PPI
points: Bolus 80 mg IV followed by 8 mg/h for 72 hours
Proven reduction in peptic rebleeding and surgery

right.title: Intermittent high-dose regimen
points: Omeprazole or pantoprazole 40 to 80 mg IV twice daily
Permits easier nursing administration and lowers cost

steps.tx: **HALT-IT** found that **tranexamic acid** did not reduce death from gastrointestinal bleeding and increased venous thrombosis. It is not given for this indication. Large-scale randomised evidence demonstrated that antifibrinolytic therapy failed to improve bleeding mortality while significantly elevating deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism in gastrointestinal haemorrhage.

Large-scale randomised evidence demonstrated that antifibrinolytic therapy failed to improve bleeding mortality while significantly elevating deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism in gastrointestinal haemorrhage.

rows: Contraindicated for routine acute GI haemorrhage

steps.tx: Early **TIPS** is considered for **Child-Pugh C** cirrhosis below 14 points, or Child-Pugh B with active bleeding, after initial control of variceal haemorrhage. Pre-emptive transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt placement within 24 to 72 hours reduces treatment failure and mortality in high-risk cirrhotic variceal bleeding.

left.title: Early pre-emptive TIPS criteria
points: Child-Pugh class C with score 10 to 13 points
Child-Pugh class B with active spurting at endoscopy
Perform within 24 to 72 hours of initial band ligation

right.title: Clinical endpoints achieved
points: Better outcome than standard rescue TIPS after failure

steps.tx: A **Sengstaken-Blakemore tube** is a bridge to endoscopy or TIPS in exsanguinating variceal bleeding. The airway is protected first. The balloon is not left inflated as definitive treatment. Tracheal intubation must precede balloon insertion, and gastric balloon traction is limited to 24 hours to prevent fatal oesophageal rupture.

rows: Mandatory to prevent aspiration of massive blood
Inflate with 250 mL air and apply 1 kg traction
Confirm intragastric placement on radiography first
Inflate only if bleeding persists (30 mmHg)
Deflate within 24 hours to avoid transmural necrosis

steps.tx: **SUP-ICU** found that **pantoprazole** did not reduce 90 day mortality in ICU patients at risk of **stress ulceration**, and it did reduce clinically important bleeding. Prophylaxis is for high risk patients, not for every ICU admission. Restricting acid suppression to mechanical ventilation over 48 hours or coagulopathy avoids nosocomial Clostridioides difficile colitis.

left.title: SUP-ICU trial results
points: Primary outcome of 90-day mortality was identical
Clinically important GI bleeding reduced from 4.2% to 2.5%
No difference in ventilator-associated pneumonia rates

right.title: Targeted prophylaxis indications
points: Invasive mechanical ventilation expected over 48 hours
Coagulopathy with platelets under 50,000 or INR over 1.5
Avoid routine universal prophylaxis in low-risk patients

steps.tx: Lower gastrointestinal bleeding is usually self limited. Unstable patients are resuscitated like upper bleeding and go to **CT angiography** when endoscopy of the stomach has not found the source. Rapid arterial phase computed tomography detects active extravasation at rates as low as 0.3 mL/min, directing catheter-directed superselective embolisation.
